why: Past call git-be9cf5dd-18: author kept the 'neural pathways' passage over nothing, because the rough first-person voice is his and the alternative reads indirectly patronizing.
A keeps the clause saying what a mismatch means, which adds real information on the why (git-d9fed027-114); B drops it.
Cuts the clever flywheel kicker and the M6 back-reference; fewer words, the point is already made.
Shorter wins when the difference is a few added words; B's 'for the pushback' and 'session's' add no information.
Shorter wins: B cuts the closing forward-hint sentence about Phase 3 and Phase 4 (low value add forward hint; what is coming next goes).
Shorter wins: B adds an orientation sentence about the course itself ('you are not learning them here'), which the author cuts as a slide-about-the-course line.
B's title names what the slide shows (where the file gets read) in plain words; A's 'Three agents' is a count that does no memory work, which the author cuts.
A names the concrete steps the student will take (orient, run checks, tests-first fix, PR, CLAUDE.local.md, ticket), which follows the preference for a concrete action; B is vaguer.
Shorter wins when a whole low-value clause is removed; A's opener 'A strong candidate for a team PR, after you talk to the team' repeats what the next bullet says.
Past call tn-loop-verb: author kept 'Loop it, instead of you starting it' over 'Run a kit skill on a schedule'; looping carries the concept and the student acts.
tn-oldskool-cut: author kept the advanced option (ccstatusline or /statusline) on a basic checkbox step; B drops it.
B's heading names the point in plain words that the body then backs with the Slack-thread example; A's heading is a longer abstract claim, so B is slightly more concrete and shorter.
A count becomes a frame the student controls when the number does no memory work; A is shorter and drops the 'Five' title.
The author keeps permission lines (AE101 'it right first time', tn-permission-testing). The line reassures the student and says why the work is an experiment.

B cuts the course-orientation sentences ('the whole map, and where you are on it', 'Everyone names a moment first…') — the author cuts slides/sentences about the course itself, forward hints and orientation repeats.
A is shorter; the added 'more entries than you want to deal with' sentence is a restatement of 'over-produces on purpose' — cut whole low-value sentences.
Cuts low-value closers ('doesn't have to be in your head', 'Nobody outside your team... theatre'); shorter wins, and 'theatre' is a loaded put-down word.
Only bolding differs; no taste rule or past call covers emphasis formatting, so neither is clearly better.
Wording identical; only bold lead-ins differ, and no taste rule or past call covers that.
